nodes.description: The files in a folder whose names match the pattern (*.png, *.jpg: * and ?, case ignored; several separated by commas), sorted, optionally in its subfolders too. Wire it into a node's file input to run that node once per file, each result labelled with the file's name.

nodes.description: Read a file into a value: an image, an SVG, a PDF or any bytes, its media type from its extension. Given a list of files (Find Files, Select Files), it reads each, so wiring its value into, say, an app's Open image input opens every file.

inputs.name: file
inputs.tooltip: The file to read; wire Find Files or Select Files to read each

nodes.description: Write values into a folder: each file is named from basename and what made the value (trace_corgi_colors-8.svg: the file it came from and the settings varied), with its type's extension. A different file already there is an error unless overwrite is on.

inputs.name: basename

inputs.name: overwrite
inputs.tooltip: Replace files that are already there

nodes.description: Rows of values (a spreadsheet's Read range, or Table to Rows) as a table of named columns, the first row the names (without a header, c1, c2, …). A column is INT, FLOAT or BOOL when every value is one, else STRING. Table to Rows goes the other way.

nodes.description: The items of a, b (and c) paired up in order, as one list of tuples: (a1, b1), (a2, b2), … The lists must be the same length; a single value goes with every item. Unzip splits the tuples again.

nodes.description: A 1-D or rows × columns array as a table, a column for each array column, named by the array's names or c1, c2, …: INT, BOOL or FLOAT as the array's type, NaN as null. The inverse of Table to Array.
A CSV file (as GridCraft exports one) as a table: the first row names the columns, and each column's type comes from its values.
An HTML file as its source text, the markup kept: UTF-8, a byte-order mark dropped.
A Markdown file as its text, the markup kept: UTF-8, a byte-order mark dropped.
A TXT file (as WordCraft or PdfCraft exports one) as text: UTF-8, a byte-order mark dropped.
A JSON value as text, indented by two spaces, keys sorted. The inverse of Text to JSON.
A table's INT and FLOAT columns as a rows × columns array (float64), named by the columns; a null is NaN, and other columns are left out. The inverse of Array to Table.
A table as CSV text, a header line first, as Table to CSV writes a file. The inverse of Text to Table.
Text that is JSON as its value. Text that isn't is an error. The inverse of JSON to Text.
CSV text as a table, as CSV to Table reads a file: the first row names the columns, and each column's type comes from its values. The inverse of Table to Text.
A table as a CSV file, a header line first. The inverse of CSV to Table.
Text (HTML source) as an HTML file, UTF-8. The inverse of HTML to Text.
Text as a Markdown file, UTF-8. The inverse of Markdown to Text.
Text as a TXT file, UTF-8. The inverse of TXT to Text.
